Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — integration + structured output reliability

Alex / Samira — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the concrete next steps we discussed: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Goal: integrate Redwood inference into Acme's document-processing pipeline for structured extraction and downstream reranking.
- Reliability requirements: JSON-schema constrained outputs for downstream parsers, validation/failover behavior on malformed responses, and a predictable retry pattern.
- Auth & infra: prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) and SSO for control plane; require options for regional routing (us-east vs eu-west).

Integration & architecture items we agreed to follow up on
1) SDK setup & auth — sample code (we'll include a starter repo). Need to know whether you prefer API keys or mTLS + KMS integration for signing requests.
2) Routing & model variants — policy for routing production traffic to smaller quantized variants for cost and falling back to higher-quality variants on SLA breach.
3) Structured output reliability — JSON schema to validate outputs, constrained decoding recommendations (token-level constraints + function/tool calling where appropriate), and validation + retry patterns (how to handle partial/malformed outputs).
4) Embeddings & reranker — typical pipeline we recommend: generate candidate spans with structured output, embed candidates, run a fast vector-reranker (embedding similarity) before final scoring.

Attachments I shared:
- redwood-integration-guide.pdf (SDK quickstart, auth options, routing examples)
- sow-draft.docx (initial SOW for pilot)
- schema.json (example constrained JSON schema for invoice extraction)

Immediate next steps
- Dylan: can you add the engineering checklist + minimal code snippets for constrained decoding + validator? (cc'ed)
- Alex / Samira: confirm preferred auth approach (API key vs mTLS/KMS) and an initial timeslot for an SE deep-dive (30–45m) next week.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Alex — adding a short tech checklist and a few practical recommendations below. I attached schema.json (expanded example) and a small snippet you can paste into your service.

Quick tech checklist
- SDK: Use our official node/python SDK. Initialize with REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or configure mutual TLS if you plan to use customer certs + KMS signing.
- Auth header: Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY> (for apiKey) or mTLS cert + signed JWT for KMS route.
- Routing: Set route_policy in request metadata {"preferred_region": "us-east-1", "fallback_model": "redwood-model-4b-fp16"}. The platform will attempt the preferred model then fallback per policy.

Structured output / constrained decoding patterns
- Prefer tool/function calling when you need strict schema. Define a function signature (JSON schema) and enable function_calling in the request; runtime will bias decoding to the schema.
- If using free-form generation: send a strict JSON schema in the prompt and enable constrained decoding (token-level constraints) + sampling settings: temperature=0.0 for deterministic outputs.
- Always run post-response validation against the schema.json. If validation fails, apply a retry with a recovery prompt (explicitly instruct model to correct format) up to N=2 times, then fallback to a human-in-the-loop step.

Example retry pattern (pseudocode)
1) call generate(payload)
2) if !validate(schema, response):
   - call generate(payload + "Return valid JSON conforming to schema X. If you cannot, reply with \"{\"error\":\"FORMAT\"}\".)
   - if still invalid after 2 retries: queue to parsing-error queue and notify CS/eng.

Embeddings & reranker notes
- Produce structured candidates (e.g., {entity, span, confidence}).
- Embed each candidate with embeddings endpoint (model: redwood-mini-embed-1).
- Use a lightweight ANN index or Faiss on your side for initial recall, then compute exact cosine on top-K for reranking.
- We generally recommend 1536-d embeddings for document reranking workloads (tradeoff: throughput vs quality).

Attached: schema.json (expanded), sample_code_snippet.txt (node/pytorch snippets). Happy to walk through the code on the SE call.

—Dylan

Alex — great questions. Quick answers and confirmation for the SE call.

1) Constrained decoding failure playbook: see attached schema.json and the exact retry prompt we use in production (included below). If the JSON is invalid after 2 retries we surface the item to a parsing-error queue and include the raw model output + validator errors for triage.

   Retry prompt (example):
   "You previously returned JSON that did not match the required schema. Please reformat your answer as valid JSON matching the following schema: <insert schema>. If you cannot produce valid JSON, reply with {\"error\":\"FORMAT\"} and include a short reason. Do not include any extra text."

2) Partial / truncated JSON: first try a constrained-recompletion with the last valid prefix + explicit "complete the JSON only" instruction. If truncated repeatedly, escalate to the fallback model variant (higher-capacity) for the request, and then fall back to human-in-the-loop if still failing.

3) Embedding throughput guidance: for 1536-d embeddings on our dedicated infra expect ~150–300 qps per A100 (depending on batching). For reranking at ~50 qps we recommend a small pool with batching enabled (batch size 16–32) and an ANN index for recall. We can provide pilot sizing suggestions once we know average candidate counts per query.
